summary.title: Nim Days: Day 11 - Bake applications (writing a build system)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small Makefile-like build tool in Nim that orders task dependencies with a topological run and detects cycles using DFS with graph coloring.
keywords: write a build system in nim
takeaways: A Makefile is made of variables, targets, and dependencies; a target runs only after its dependencies.
Tasks and their dependencies can be stored as an adjacency list (Table of name to required task names) plus a table mapping names to task objects.
Running a task means recursively walking its dependencies, skipping already-seen tasks, and echoing actions in dependency order.
Cycles are detected with DFS and three vertex colors (white, gray, black); reaching a gray vertex means a back edge and a cycle.
summary.summary: This is Day 11 of a Nim blog series in which the author builds a small task runner called Bake, similar to a Makefile. The post covers the basic model of variables, targets and dependencies, then shows example API usage for adding tasks and running them, including a circular dependency example. The implementation section explains using an adjacency list for the task graph, a recursive helper that produces an ordered list of tasks while skipping seen ones, and a DFS-based cycle check that uses white, gray and black node colors. The post ends with listed next steps such as variable support, YAML recipes, and Ansible-like modules.
